rationale: Start with a broad scouting gradient that spans almost the full organic range so all 10 compounds are likely to elute and map their elution window. A midrange temperature and moderate gradient time balance getting informative spacing with avoiding excessive truncation on the first run.

All pairs are already fully resolved, so the only score loss is the late last peak; the first run implies the compounds elute over roughly phi_e 0.11 to 0.59, so trim the gradient to that window and shorten it to pull the last peak earlier while keeping peaks inside the gradient. Keep temperature fixed to isolate the effect of the phi window and gradient time on total runtime and resolution.

Resolution still has ample margin, so push for a shorter last-peak time by making the gradient slightly steeper and starting a bit stronger while keeping the late peak within the gradient window. This should test how much runtime can be cut before the tight mid-cluster near peaks 5–7 begins to lose resolution.

Keeping composition and temperature fixed cleanly tests whether this critical pair is slope-sensitive enough to reach full credit.

This tests whether that critical pair responds more to the phi window than to pure slope or temperature.

The data suggest the critical pair is highly temperature-selective and worsens on both sides of 40 C, so test the remaining lower adjacent setting to map that behavior more completely. Although likely not optimal, a 30 C run can reveal whether the selectivity trend is monotonic or whether a different close-pair arrangement emerges that informs the final local search.

Use the fully resolved 10 min condition but narrow the upper end of the gradient window to keep the late peak from eluting as late as it did at phi1 0.60.
